topic.angle: How patterns are printed onto silicon with light and photoresist

panels.text: A chip starts as a silicon wafer. It is coated with a photoresist, a material that reacts to light.
A photomask carrying the pattern is placed over the wafer, and light is shone through it. Only some areas of the photoresist are exposed.
The exposed areas undergo a chemical change. A developer solution then washes away either the exposed or the unexposed parts, leaving the pattern behind.
That pattern guides etching, deposition or ion implantation to build the circuit. The twist: one technique, EUV lithography, uses extreme ultraviolet light with a wavelength of 13.5 nm.
